source: NCERT Class X, Science, Ch. 12 (Magnetic Effects of Electric Current).

sections.heading: 1. Magnetic Field and Field Lines
points: A **magnet** has two poles (north, south); like poles repel, unlike attract.
A **magnetic field** is the region around a magnet where its force acts; represented by **magnetic field lines** (from N to S outside the magnet).
Field lines never cross; closer lines = stronger field; a **compass needle** aligns along field lines.
**Oersted's discovery** — a current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it.

sections.heading: 2. Field due to Current
points: **Straight conductor** — field lines are **concentric circles**; direction by **right-hand thumb rule** (thumb = current, fingers = field).
Field strength ∝ current, and decreases with distance from the wire.
**Circular loop** — field at the centre is stronger; adds up with more turns.
**Solenoid** — a coil acts like a **bar magnet**; produces a uniform field inside; used to make **electromagnets** (a soft iron core magnetised by current).

sections.heading: 3. Force on a Conductor and the Electric Motor
points: A **current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force** (largest when current ⊥ field).
Direction given by **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule** (thumb = force/motion, forefinger = field, middle finger = current).
**Electric motor** — converts electrical energy to **mechanical energy**; uses a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field (with a **split-ring commutator** to reverse current each half-rotation).

sections.heading: 4. Electromagnetic Induction and Generator
points: **Electromagnetic induction (Faraday)** — a changing magnetic field near a coil **induces a current** in it.
Direction of induced current: **Fleming's Right-Hand Rule** (thumb = motion, forefinger = field, middle = induced current).
**Electric generator (dynamo)** — converts **mechanical energy to electrical energy** (AC or DC using rings/commutator).
**AC (alternating current)** reverses direction periodically (India: 50 Hz, changes every 1/100 s); **DC (direct current)** flows one way; AC is easier to transmit over long distances.
**Domestic circuits:** live (red/brown), neutral (black/blue), earth (green — safety); **fuse** and **earthing** protect against short circuits/overload.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Oersted: current produces a magnetic field; field lines go N→S outside.
Straight wire → concentric circles (right-hand thumb rule).
Motor: electrical → mechanical (split-ring commutator); Fleming's Left-Hand Rule = force.
Generator: mechanical → electrical (electromagnetic induction, Faraday); Right-Hand Rule = induced current.
AC in India = 50 Hz; earth wire (green) = safety; fuse protects circuit.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Motor = electrical → mechanical**; **Generator = mechanical → electrical** (do not swap).
**Fleming's Left-Hand Rule** = force on conductor (motor); **Right-Hand Rule** = induced current (generator).
**AC frequency in India = 50 Hz** (reverses every 1/100 second).
The **earth wire (green)** is a safety measure; the **fuse** guards against overload.
